definition: Mechanisms that allow an AI agent to store and later retrieve information across interactions, extending beyond what fits in a single context window.
details: Agent memory systems can include short-term working memory (within a session) and long-term memory (persisted across sessions), often implemented using external storage combined with retrieval mechanisms.

explainer.lead: Mechanisms that allow an AI agent to store and later retrieve information across interactions, extending beyond what fits in a single context window. It lets agents carry knowledge from one session into another.

tiers.eli5: The agent writes notes so it can remember your earlier conversations even after its short-term memory fills up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers implement agent memory as short-term working memory within a session and long-term memory persisted across sessions, often using external storage combined with retrieval.
tiers.paperLevel: Mechanisms that allow an AI agent to store and later retrieve information across interactions, extending beyond a single context window; systems can include short-term working memory (within a session) and long-term memory (persisted across sessions).

explainer.example: An agent stores a user's preference in external storage and retrieves it in a later session when relevant.
